The key difference from L40S llama at 2.1% (where 4/5 failed): A100-SXM's absolute fitness landscape is higher and the threshold (0.137432 = 0.99×0.138820) is crossed by multiple TP4/2inst configurations — not just the max-profile config. This reveals that TPE convergence at tight margins depends on BOTH relative margin width AND hardware-specific landscape structure (how many configs fall above the threshold).

discrepancy_analysis: Three of four arms confirmed; h-ablation partially confirmed with a magnitude discrepancy. The main unexpected finding: flat TPE on A100-SXM at 1.07% TP margin (the tightest TP=4 margin in the campaign) is NOT a failure regime — all 5 seeds pass the within-1% threshold with median evals_to_best=26. This contrasts with L40S llama at 2.1% margin where 4/5 seeds failed. The implication is that the TPE convergence threshold is hardware/model-specific: A100-SXM qwen's landscape allows more configurations to exceed the threshold than L40S llama's. The [2.1%, 5.1%] bound from RP-22 is specific to L40S hardware and cannot be universally applied. Within A100-SXM (same hardware, different seeds): margin width still has a strong causal effect on convergence speed (median evals_to_best 26 vs 6 at 1.07% vs 4.47% margin).
